features.description: Environmental control + per-supervisor ExecutionEnvironment isolation. Plan-level target_env/target_project contract, command guards, isolated tool-state namespaces (gcloud/firebase/xcodebuild/android/kubectl/gh/npm/docker/terraform), forbid project-mutating commands, prod gate. Hard-blocks F009-F014 (cross-project work) and any production deploy automation. EC10 generalized from CLOUDSDK_CONFIG-only to per-supervisor ExecutionEnvironment per Codex audit D065.
steps: EC1: environments.json per consumer repo: maps {dev,staging,prod} to firebase_project, gcp_project, xcode_scheme, bundle_id, hosting_target, allowed_deploy_commands[], requires_gates[]
EC2: target_env + target_project contract in plan.md (visible Target section + Python validator until schema v1.1)
EC3: command_guard.py — preflight + post-hoc check: reject bare side-effect commands missing explicit project/scheme/destination/branch flags

EC4: ExecutionEnvironment per dispatch — supervisor injects env vars (CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT, FIREBASE_PROJECT, JARVIS_TARGET_ENV, JARVIS_TARGET_PROJECT) so agents read declared target, not ambient shell state
EC5: prompt rule — agents must declare {repo, env, project, command} before any side-effect call; auditor verifies against plan.target_env
EC6: audit field target_context: {env, project, commands_run[]}; supervisor rejects audits whose target_context.env != plan.target_env
EC7: prod gate — target_env=prod requires pre_impl AND on_escalation in human_gates regardless of tier; supervisor refuses to dispatch otherwise
EC8: starter environments.json files for Jarvis (<firebase-project-id>), Glam, SpinDine, axiom

EC9: forbid project-mutating commands — command_guard hard-rejects regardless of context: gcloud config set project, gcloud config configurations activate (without CLOUDSDK_CONFIG), firebase use --add, kubectl config use-context, gh auth switch, npm config set, git config --global, etc.

EC10 (generalized): per-supervisor ExecutionEnvironment isolation — supervisor mints per-plan temp dirs and points each tool's config namespace at them: CLOUDSDK_CONFIG, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, CONFIGSTORE_DIR, KUBECONFIG, GH_CONFIG_DIR, NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG, DOCKER_CONFIG, GRADLE_USER_HOME, ANDROID_USER_HOME, ANDROID_AVD_HOME, TF_DATA_DIR. Tool-specific flag discipline (xcodebuild explicit -scheme/-configuration/-destination/-derivedDataPath; gradle explicit flavor/buildType + --gradle-user-home). Mutations stay sandboxed; parallel supervisors against same/different projects are safe. Cleanup on volley terminate.
EC11: per-plan .firebaserc + cwd discipline — supervisor CDs into plan working dir before firebase invocations; --project flag always passed

EC12: vendor coverage — explicit isolation per CLI: gcloud (CLOUDSDK_CONFIG + --project / CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT, forbid gcloud config set project), firebase (--project + isolated XDG/configstore, forbid firebase use), xcodebuild (explicit -scheme/-configuration/-destination/-derivedDataPath, no shared simulator without UDID reservation), android/gradle (explicit flavor/buildType + isolated GRADLE_USER_HOME, no shared emulator without reservation), kubectl (KUBECONFIG + --context, forbid kubectl config use-context), gh (GH_CONFIG_DIR or GH_TOKEN, forbid gh auth switch), npm/yarn/pnpm (isolated user config/cache, forbid registry mutation), git (worktree per plan, branch locks, forbid git config --global, gate dangerous push forms), docker (DOCKER_CONFIG + explicit context), terraform (TF_DATA_DIR + explicit workspace/backend)

EC13: active-supervisor registry at ~/.jarvis/active_supervisors.jsonl with PID, plan_id, target_project, target_env, started_at, supervisor_config_dir; jarvis ps lists running supervisors; re-entrancy warning on same plan_id; cleanup via atexit

Plan validator rejects plans missing target_env, and rejects target_env=prod plans missing pre_impl + on_escalation gates. Real volley with target_env=dev produces audit JSONs whose target_context.env==dev. environments.json starter files exist for Jarvis + at least one consumer (Glam or SpinDine).
